# Jack Homer

> Jack Homer is a Forward Deployed Engineer at C3 AI in Redwood City, California, and a technical lead across U.S. Marine Corps enterprise AI programs. He builds production multi-agent systems and agentic developer tooling. He holds a B.S. in computer science from Virginia Tech and lives in the San Francisco Bay Area. jackhomer.com is his personal site.

Not to be confused with other people named Jack Homer: this is the software engineer at C3 AI (GitHub: jhomer192).

## About

- [About Jack Homer](https://jackhomer.com/about/): who he is, what he does, where he studied
- [Career](https://jackhomer.com/career/): forward-deployed engineering at C3 AI, including Marine Corps workforce and logistics applications, a multi-agent legal-document translation pipeline, and an agentic ticket-to-pull-request harness
- [Tableside](https://jackhomer.com/business/): his small web studio for local businesses
- [Contact](https://jackhomer.com/contact/)

## Side projects

- [Apartment Finder](https://jackhomer.com/projects/apartment-finder/): A private, password-protected apartment search for roommates in San Francisco: nightly crawl, scam-risk scoring, neighborhood data.
- [Auto Applier](https://jackhomer.com/projects/auto-applier/): Text a job link to a Telegram bot, and an agent reads the posting, fills out the application and submits it.
- [Backpressure](https://jackhomer.com/projects/backpressure/): Practice system-design interviews solo. Diagram on a canvas, answer an AI interviewer's questions, and read a scored verdict. Free and open source.
- [Birthday Paradox](https://jackhomer.com/projects/birthday-paradox/): The theoretical probability curve and a live in-browser Monte Carlo simulator, side by side, showing why 23 people is enough for a shared birthday.
- [Tabletop Portal](https://jackhomer.com/projects/board-game-portal/): A directory of board games playable online, filtered by player count, time and complexity, each linking to the best existing implementation.
- [Call It](https://jackhomer.com/projects/call-it/): Prediction markets for a group of friends, played with points, never money. Start a league, invite friends by link, and trade on the answers.
- [Claude Discord](https://jackhomer.com/projects/claude-bot/): Self-hostable Claude bots in a private Discord server, one process per bot, a live session per channel, and hand-off between bots by mention.
- [Clocktower ST](https://jackhomer.com/projects/clocktower/): A Storyteller's control panel for Blood on the Clocktower that runs setup, night order, and voting so you can focus on the table.
- [Color Analysis](https://jackhomer.com/projects/color-analysis/): Upload a portrait, get a 12-season analysis with palette, hair and makeup direction from Claude vision.
- [Connections Maker](https://jackhomer.com/projects/connections-maker/): Build your own NYT Connections-style word puzzle and share it with a single link, no account or backend required.
- [Flight Deals](https://jackhomer.com/projects/flight-deals/): A fare-watch prototype running on simulated prices: watches, a deal feed and 30-day price history. A prototype of the interface, not a booking tool.
- [Game of Life](https://jackhomer.com/projects/game-of-life/): An interactive Conway's Game of Life that runs at up to 60 generations a second on a wrap-around canvas, with a pattern library and live stats.
- [Hanabi](https://jackhomer.com/projects/hanabi/): The cooperative fireworks card game for iPhone, built for a private group: invite-only sign-in by email, with Claude bots and post-game coaching.
- [Holdbreaker](https://jackhomer.com/projects/holdbreaker/): A phone app that waits on hold for you and rings you when a person picks up. In private testing on a simulated line; not public.
- [Hotel Finder](https://jackhomer.com/projects/hotel-finder/): Hotels from OpenStreetMap in 49 cities, on a map with star filters and booking links. Up to 200 per city, no API key. Shows locations, not prices.
- [Meme Maker](https://jackhomer.com/projects/meme-maker/): A browser meme editor: pick a template or drop in your own image, caption it, and download a clean PNG. No backend, no uploads, no watermark.
- [Nuzlocke](https://jackhomer.com/projects/nuzlocke/): A run tracker for Pokémon Nuzlocke challenges: every route encounter, your living team, the graveyard, badges, and boss prep in one place.
- [Pokémon Agent](https://jackhomer.com/projects/pokemon-agent/): A multi-agent system of local models on his own GPU plays Pokémon FireRed and Emerald unassisted, one button press at a time.
- [Polygon Stickers](https://jackhomer.com/projects/polygon-stickers/): Polygon Stickers turns a photo into an iOS sticker in the browser with a magic wand, brushes, and on-device background removal. No App Store, no developer account.
- [Secrets Vault](https://jackhomer.com/projects/secrets-vault/): A personal secrets manager that lets AI coding agents use credentials without printing them, with a Face ID iPhone app. Private, not a product.
- [Songrank](https://jackhomer.com/projects/songrank/): Rank your most-played Spotify tracks through head-to-head comparisons, then export the result as a real playlist.
- [Sticker Maker](https://jackhomer.com/projects/sticker-maker/): Cut anything out of a photo and turn it into a sticker, in the browser with no account. Exports sized for Discord, Telegram and WhatsApp.
- [WikiGame](https://jackhomer.com/projects/wikigame/): WikiGame is a daily Wikipedia race: the same two articles for everyone, only in-page links to get between them, and a solver bot that sets your par.
- [Wikipedia Game Solver](https://jackhomer.com/projects/wikipedia-game-solver/): Wikipedia Game Solver walks the links from one Wikipedia article to another by text similarity, or runs a bidirectional search for the shortest path.
